draft.title: Antibiotics and antivirals
card: Antibiotic
a drug that kills bacteria or stops them growing. It does nothing to viruses, so it cannot treat a cold or flu.
Antiviral
a drug that slows a virus, for example by limiting how fast it copies itself inside host cells. Each antiviral works on particular viruses.
Resistance
In a population of bacteria, a few may carry a gene that lets them survive an antibiotic. The drug kills the others, so the survivors reproduce and pass on the gene.
Overuse
Using antibiotics when they are not needed, or not finishing a course, gives more chances for resistant bacteria to be selected. Infections then become harder to treat.
draft.remember: Antibiotics target bacteria, antivirals slow viruses, and overusing antibiotics selects for resistant bacteria.

a.q: Why is an antibiotic not a suitable treatment for influenza?
opts: Influenza is caused by a virus, which antibiotics do not affect
Influenza is caused by bacteria that are already resistant
Antibiotics only work on the body's memory cells
Antibiotics speed up the copying of viruses
a.why: Influenza is caused by a virus, and antibiotics act on bacteria, not viruses. Resistance is a tempting answer, but it applies to bacteria that have been exposed to antibiotics, and influenza is not a bacterial infection.
a.clue: Think about what type of pathogen causes influenza.

b.q: A clinic in Bathurst gives antibiotics to many patients with mild infections that did not need them. Over several years, more infections no longer respond to the drugs. What best explains this?
opts: The drugs killed other bacteria, so resistant ones survived and spread
The drugs made each bacterium change itself to become resistant
The drugs turned the bacteria into viruses that drugs cannot treat
Patients' bodies became unable to respond to any drug
b.why: Bacteria with a resistance gene survive the drug, reproduce and pass the gene on, so resistant bacteria become more common. The tempting wrong answer says each bacterium changes itself in response. The drug selects bacteria that already carry the gene.
b.clue: Ask which bacteria survive the drug and what they then do.

proposal.title: Antibiotics and antivirals
card: Antibiotic
a drug that kills bacteria or stops them growing. It does nothing to viruses, so it cannot treat a cold or flu.

Resistance
In a population of bacteria, a few may carry a gene that lets them survive an antibiotic. The drug kills the others, so the survivors reproduce and pass on the gene.
Overuse

Using antibiotics when they are not needed, such as for a viral infection, adds to the bacteria's total exposure to the drugs. More exposure selects for more resistant bacteria, so infections become harder to treat.
